verses.1: How the LORD has consumed in His anger the daughter of Zion! He has thrown from the heavens to the earth the glory of Israel; He has not remembered His footstool in the day of His anger.
verses.2: The LORD has devoured without mercy all the beauty of Jacob; He has shattered the strongholds of the daughter of Judah. He has brought her down to the ground, defiled the kingdom and its rulers.
verses.3: He has cut off every horn of Israel, turned back His right hand from the face of the enemy. He has burned in Jacob like a consuming fire, devouring all around.
verses.4: He has drawn His bow like an enemy, held up His right hand like an adversary. He has slain all the delights of the eye, the tents of the daughter of Zion. He has poured out His wrath like fire.
verses.5: The LORD has become like an enemy, devouring Israel, devouring all her palaces. He has broken down her strongholds, multiplying sorrow and distress for the daughter of Judah.
verses.6: He has spread her like a garden under siege, destroyed her feasts. The LORD has forgotten in Zion the appointed times and the Sabbath; He has despised His king and His priests in a fury of anger.
verses.7: The LORD has abandoned His altar, defiled His sanctuary. He has handed over the gates of her strongholds to the enemy. He has raised a cry in the house of the LORD, as in the day of the feast.
verses.8: The LORD has plotted to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion. He has stretched the line, He has not withdrawn His hand from destruction. He has mourned both rampart and wall; they have languished together.
verses.9: Her gates have sunk into the ground; He has destroyed and broken her bars. Her king and her rulers are among the nations, finding no law. Her prophets have found no vision from the LORD.
verses.10: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have sprinkled dust on their heads, wrapped themselves in sackcloth, and bowed their heads toward the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.11: My eyes have failed from weeping; my heart has been shaken. My strength has poured out to the ground, over the ruin of the daughter of my people. The infant and the nursing child have fallen in the streets of the city.
verses.12: They say to their mothers, “Where is grain and wine?” As they lie wrapped like the dead in the streets, their lives are poured out into the lap of their mothers.
verses.13: How can I comfort you, O daughter of Jerusalem? To what should I compare you? What should I liken to you, O virgin daughter of Zion? For your ruin is as vast as the sea; who can heal you?
verses.14: Your prophets have shown you falsehood and futility; they did not reveal your iniquity to turn your captivity. Instead, they showed you empty visions and deceptive divinations.
verses.15: All who pass by clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem. “This is the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth.”
verses.16: All your enemies open their mouths wide over you; they hiss and gnash their teeth. “We have devoured her,” they say. “This is the day we longed for. We have found it, we have seen it.”
verses.17: The LORD has done what He purposed; He has fulfilled His decree, which He declared from ancient times. He has brought it to pass, showing no mercy. He has made your enemies rejoice over you, raised the horn of your adversaries.
verses.18: The heart of the daughter of Zion cried out to the LORD. “Let tears flow like a river by day and by night; let them not cease. Let there be no rest for her eyes, no sleep for her head.”
verses.19: Arise in the night, cry out at the head of the watchtowers. Pour out your heart like water before the face of the LORD. Lift your hands to Him for the lives of your infants, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.
verses.20: Look, O LORD, and see to whom You have done this. Should women eat the fruit of their womb, the infants who are dandled? Should a priest and a prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the LORD?
verses.21: The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets. My virgins and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have slain in Your day of anger; You have not shown mercy.
verses.22: You summoned a day like an appointed feast, surrounding me on every side. There was no escape in the day of the LORD’s anger. I did not raise a child or nurture a son, yet now my enemies have consumed them all.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "the daughter of Zion" — a poetic reference to Jerusalem, used consistently in the book.  
- v. 4: "the tents of the daughter of Zion" — likely metaphorical for the dwellings or sacred spaces of the city.  
- v. 13: "To what should I compare you?" — reflects the poetic device of rhetorical questioning for emphasis.  
- v. 14: "empty visions and deceptive divinations" — the Hebrew is clear in condemning false prophecy.  
- v. 19: "at the head of the watchtowers" — a reference to the high places or fortified points of the city.  
- v. 20: "fruit of their womb" — refers to children, as in Leviticus 26:29.  
- v. 21: "by the sword" — clear, but the Hebrew may imply both literal and metaphorical destruction.
